name: Cable Low Fly
movementPattern: Shoulder flexion and horizontal adduction - low-to-high arc
grip: Supinated or semi-supinated grip holding single D-handles, palms facing forward and upward.
description: Sweep dual low-cable handles upward and inward along a diagonal lifting arc toward upper-chest or chin height in a standing staggered stance, emphasizing the clavicular fibers of the pectoralis major.
setup: Set two cable pulleys to their lowest positions and attach a single D-handle to each.
Grasp a handle in each hand with palms facing forward/upward and step forward into an athletic staggered stance.
Stand tall with chest lifted, slight forward torso angle, and arms down and slightly back at your sides with elbows softly bent.
instructions: Sweep both handles upward and inward in an arc toward the center line until your hands meet in front of your upper chest or chin level.
Maintain a fixed, soft bend in your elbows throughout the movement (do not curl or press).
Squeeze your upper pectorals firmly for a moment at peak contraction.
Lower your arms slowly under control along the same diagonal path back to the starting stretch.
cues: Scoop upward and inward with elbows soft.
Squeeze upper chest at chin level.
commonMistakes: Bending elbows into a biceps curl instead of maintaining a wide fly arc.
Leaning the torso backward to swing the cables upward.
Using excessive shoulder shrugging at the top.

logging.example: Weight pins set to 10 kg on each low pulley: record 10 kg per cable stack.
logging.note: Dual cable stations use independent weight stacks; record selected stack pin load per side.

variantNote: Low-to-high standing cable chest fly originating from floor-level pulleys, aligning the diagonal resistance line with the clavicular pectoral fiber orientation.
reviewNotes: Drafted from FitTrack ID 52 (Cable Low Fly).
Direct counterpart to Cable High Fly; accurately pairs low-to-high line of action with clavicular chest recruitment.
